Convert a kinship2 or Pedixplorer pedigree object to the package's data frames

Source: R/asPedFrame.R
asPedFrame.Rd

Turns a kinship2 pedigree or pedigreeList object, or a Pedixplorer Pedigree object, back into the data frames the rest of the package takes: a pedigree with one row per animal, a table of twin pairs and a table of declared matings; and its layout hints into the form makePedigreeMatingLayout() takes.

Usage

asPedFrame(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
asPedFrame(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'pedigree'
asPedFrame(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'pedigreeList'
asPedFrame(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'Pedigree'
asPedFrame(x, ...)

Arguments

x

a kinship2 pedigree or pedigreeList object, or a Pedixplorer Pedigree object.

...

not used.

Value

A list of four:

ped

a data frame with the character columns id, sire, dam (an unknown parent is NA) and sex; then famid for a pedigreeList or a Pedigree with families; then the condition columns; then status; and, for a Pedigree, Pedixplorer's fields that hold data and the object's other columns.

twinRelations

a data frame with the character columns id1, id2 and code ("MZ twin", "DZ twin" or "UZ twin"), or NULL when the object has no twin pair.

hints

the object's layout hints as a list of order (numbers named by id) and mate (a data frame of left, right and anchor), each only when the object holds it, or NULL when it holds none.

matings

a data frame with the character columns sire and dam, one row per spouse pair the object holds, or NULL when it holds none.

Details

kinship2 objects. The rows keep the object's order, which is the order the animals were given to kinship2::pedigree(). Each parent is read by its own index, so an unknown parent (index 0) never moves another animal's parent. Ids become text: a factor's labels, and whole numbers written in full ("100000", not "1e+05"), so no id is renamed.

Sex becomes M, F or U: male, female, and unknown or terminated. kinship2 has no code for a hermaphrodite, so an animal entered as H comes back U. A single affected vector becomes the column affected; the columns of an affected matrix become affected_<column name>, or affected_1, affected_2 and so on when the matrix has no column names. Their values stay as kinship2 holds them: 0, 1 or NA. A status of 1 becomes "DECEASED" and 0 "ALIVE". An object with no affected or no status gives no such column. kinship2 keeps no other column, so names, dates and the like are not in its objects to convert.

Twin pairs come from the object's relation codes 1, 2 and 3 (MZ, DZ and UZ twins), and declared matings from its code 4, a spouse pair, whether kinship2 stored them as numbers or as text.

A pedigreeList (several families) is converted whole when no id appears in two families, with a famid column naming each animal's family. When ids repeat across families, asPedFrame() stops and names them (ten at most, in byte order); one family, such as x["2"], is a pedigree and converts on its own.

A kinship2 object is a plain list, so it is read without calling kinship2: kinship2 need not be installed, for an object read back from a file for instance. asPedFrame() stops for a pedigree or pedigreeList that lacks a part it needs (id, findex, mindex, sex, and famid for a pedigreeList), naming the parts.

Pedixplorer objects. A Pedigree is read through Pedixplorer's own functions, so Pedixplorer must be installed; asPedFrame() stops, saying so, when it is not. The rows keep the object's order. Ids and parents are as the object holds them: when it has families, Pedixplorer has joined each id to its family ("F1_A"), and a famid column names each animal's family. Sex becomes M, F or U (Pedixplorer, too, holds a hermaphrodite as unknown).

Each condition Pedixplorer holds (one row of fill(x) and its <name>_mods column) becomes a column with 0, 1 or NA: Pedixplorer's default condition affection, the name it gives a column affected, becomes affected; a condition whose name starts with affected keeps it; any other becomes affected_<name>. A condition with no known value is left out: an object built with no condition still holds an all-NA affection, and that is not a condition. The death status becomes status: "DECEASED", "ALIVE", or NA where it is unknown, with no column when every value is unknown.

Then come those of Pedixplorer's fields fertility, miscarriage, avail, evaluated, consultand, proband, carrier, asymptomatic, adopted, dateofbirth and dateofdeath that hold anything besides the value Pedixplorer fills in when none is given, under their own names and types (Pedixplorer keeps a birth column it is given as dateofbirth, as text). Last come the object's other columns, of its mcols(), as they are, less Pedixplorer's own (error, and each condition's and the availability's columns). asPedFrame() stops when a column name would appear twice (an extra column called sire, say), naming it. Twin pairs are the MZ, DZ and UZ twins of rel(x), and declared matings its "Spouse" rows.

Declared matings. Each spouse pair of either package becomes a row of matings, a data frame of sire and dam in the form makePedigreeMatingLayout(matings = ) and getMatings(matings = ) take: two animals mated, whether or not they have offspring together. Every row the object holds is kept, in the object's order, a pair with offspring together (which the layout and getMatings() set aside) and a pair kinship2 holds twice (Pedixplorer refuses one) included, so a table converted to either package and back is the same. When one of the two is male and the other not, the male is the sire; otherwise, when one is female and the other not, the female is the dam; otherwise the two are in the order the object holds them, which for Pedixplorer is sorted by id.

Layout hints. An object's layout hints come back in the form makePedigreeMatingLayout() takes, so makePedigreeMatingLayout(x$ped, hints = x$hints, matings = x$matings) draws with them and with the object's matings, once x$ped has its generations (findGeneration()). kinship2 keeps them in the object's hints element, which a user sets, to kinship2::autohint()'s result for instance: its order, one number per animal in the object's order, becomes order, the numbers named by id (an NA leaves that animal unnumbered); its spouse rows (the places of the left and the right animal and an anchor, 1 left, 2 right, 0 either) become mate, a data frame of the ids left and right and the anchor "left", "right" or "either". A pedigreeList's hints are read the same way, one number per animal of the whole list. asPedFrame() stops, saying what is wrong, when they cannot be read as ids: hints that are not a list, an order that is not numbers or not one per animal, or a spouse table that is not three columns of whole numbers, places from 1 to the number of animals and an anchor 1, 2 or 0. Pedixplorer keeps them in the object's hints, horder() (already named by id) and spouse(), read the same way.

Both packages make their automatic hints for their own layouts, and some of the mate rows are ones makePedigreeMatingLayout() refuses. asPedFrame() fixes them and one message names each change: a pair with no offspring together that the object does not declare mated is left out (the layout draws a mating only from offspring or from matings); a pair named in an earlier row is left out, the first row kept (as kinship2 keeps it); and an anchor on the partner of the earlier generation (findGeneration()) becomes "either", its side kept, since the layout draws a mating on the row of its later partner.

asPedFrame() stops for an object of any other class, naming the class.

See also

checkPedigree, checkTwinRelations, drawPedigreeDiagram

Examples

if (requireNamespace("kinship2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ## A and B are the parents of C and D, DZ twins; A has died and C is
  ## affected.
  p <- kinship2::pedigree(
    id = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),
    dadid = c(NA, NA, "A", "A"),
    momid = c(NA, NA, "B", "B"),
    sex = c("male", "female", "male", "female"),
    affected = c(0, 0, 1, 0),
    status = c(1, 0, 0, 0),
    relation = data.frame(id1 = "C", id2 = "D", code = 2)
  )
  asPedFrame(p)
  ## A layout hint: D drawn left of C.
  p$hints <- list(order = c(1, 2, 4, 3))
  asPedFrame(p)$hints
  ## E and F, with no offspring, declared mates (relation code 4): F, the
  ## male, is the sire.
  p <- kinship2::pedigree(
    id = c("A", "B", "C", "E", "F"),
    dadid = c(NA, NA, "A", NA, NA),
    momid = c(NA, NA, "B", NA, NA),
    sex = c("male", "female", "male", "female", "male"),
    relation = data.frame(id1 = "E", id2 = "F", code = 4)
  )
  asPedFrame(p)$matings
}
#>   sire dam
#> 1    F   E
if (requireNamespace("Pedixplorer", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ## The same family as a Pedixplorer object, with a name for each animal.
  p <- Pedixplorer::Pedigree(data.frame(
    id = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),
    dadid = c(NA, NA, "A", "A"),
    momid = c(NA, NA, "B", "B"),
    sex = c("male", "female", "male", "female"),
    affected = c(0, 0, 1, 0),
    status = c(1, 0, 0, 0),
    name = c("Al", "Bea", "Cy", "Di")
  ), rel_df = data.frame(id1 = "C", id2 = "D", code = 2))
  asPedFrame(p)
}
#> $ped
#>   id sire  dam sex affected   status name
#> 1  A <NA> <NA>   M        0 DECEASED   Al
#> 2  B <NA> <NA>   F        0    ALIVE  Bea
#> 3  C    A    B   M        1    ALIVE   Cy
#> 4  D    A    B   F        0    ALIVE   Di
#> 
#> $twinRelations
#>   id1 id2    code
#> 1   C   D DZ twin
#> 
#> $hints
#> NULL
#> 
#> $matings
#> NULL
#>
